summary.title: Accurate, Interdisciplinary and Transparent Structure-property Understanding with Deep Native Structural Reasoning (SciReasoner)

details: Structure-property understanding requires both domain-native structural representation and inspectable, evidence-linked reasoning; LLMs flatten structures into text while domain specialists output opaque scores.

SciReasoner: a single autoregressive LLM (Qwen3-14B backbone) with a unified structure-aware vocabulary that discretizes protein 3D structure (Foldseek 3Di), 3D molecular conformers (ConfSeq) and periodic crystals (SLICES) into dedicated tokens with their own embedding table, so structural tokens are cited as addressable evidence units inside generated chain-of-thought.

Self-bootstrapped native structural reasoning post-training: intra-domain structural evidence grounding (per-domain expert SFT + RL) whose on-policy traces then replace external teacher traces for a unified cross-domain coldstart + RL consolidation.

Interleaved structure-text corpora: UniProt/PDB/AlphaFoldDB proteins with 3Di tokens (pLDDT<70 masked), ChEMBL/BindingDB RDKit conformers, crystals from Materials Project, JARVIS, SNUMAT, hMOF, QMOF, OQMD, GNoME, Cantor HEA; DNA (NCBI 1kb fragments), RNA (RNAcentral); plus general web text and instruction data (Nemotron-CC v2, Dolci-Think-SFT, SciIF).

Three-stage continued pretraining: Stage 1 warm-up with frozen backbone (only new structural vocab, embeddings, head), Stage 2 full-parameter with shared WSD schedule, Stage 3 annealing with more QA data.
Leakage control: proteins >30% MMseqs2 identity to test sets removed; USPTO-50K test products and materials val/test samples removed.
Coldstart SFT with <think> traces and /no_think dual-mode responses, response-only loss masking.
DAPO RL (clip-higher, dynamic sampling, token-level reduction) with 'reward softening' mapping heterogeneous metrics (distance-based, matching-based, tool-verified) to [0,1].
RL data selection: 8 rollouts per example from the base model, keep empirical solve rate in (0.125, 0.875), sample 2000 examples per sub-task closest to p=0.5.
86 benchmarks over proteins, DNA/RNA, small molecules, crystals covering QA, property regression/classification, generation/design.
Frontier generalist LLMs: Opus-4.7, GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi-K2.6 (retrosynthesis five-shot for Opus).

Specialists: SaProt/SaprotHub, ESM2, BLAST, Foldseek, DeepFRI-GO setup, RSGPT and 18 retrosynthesis baselines, ConfSeq and 9 virtual-screening methods on 102 DUD-E targets, CGCNN, LLM-Prop, NT, MolCLR.
Structure-ablation (with vs without structural tokens) on materials, protein and small-molecule tasks, with paired reasoning-trace comparisons and residue attention maps.
GO results stratified into seven BLAST identity bins; attention from generated GO:0003677 token vs contact-defined DNA-binding sites (AUROC, top-20% enrichment).
Pass@1 vs pass@10 across four post-training stages; LLM-as-judge (GPT-5.5) rubric scoring of traces (100 records/task).
Double-blind human expert evaluation, N=177 case-judgements over GO annotation, materials property, retrosynthesis, five-axis 1-10 rubric plus pairwise preference.

key_findings.finding: Native structural tokenization plus self-bootstrapped reasoning yields specialist-level or better accuracy across a very broad multimodal scientific benchmark suite from one autoregressive model.
key_findings.evidence: SOTA on 67 of 86 benchmarks; matches or exceeds published specialists on 26 of 33 tasks with such baselines; best among four frontier LLMs on 75/86; examples include DeepFRI-GO mean Fmax 0.59 vs SaProt 0.52, subcellular localization 0.88 vs ESM2 0.84, Isoform R2 0.86 vs 0.59, formation-energy parity R2=0.895.

key_findings.finding: Gains are largest where homology or template shortcuts fail, indicating structure-grounded rather than memorized inference.
key_findings.evidence: In the Cellular Component (0,30]% BLAST identity bin, Fmax 0.55 vs 0.34 for BLAST (+0.21) and 0.42 for ESM2 (+0.13); GPT-5.5 judge reasoning-quality scores remain stable across all seven similarity bins and above coldstart and DeepSeek-V4-Pro.

key_findings.finding: Structural evidence is causally necessary for the model's reasoning, not just an extra input channel.
key_findings.evidence: Structure-ablation lowers performance across materials, protein and molecule tasks (e.g. larger absolute errors for bandgap, largest-cavity- and pore-limiting-diameter); without structure, traces fall back on composition/sequence priors (QMOF pore size overestimated by nearly an order of magnitude; GO trace diverted to DNA recombination), and attention shifts away from binding sites; PCA shows SciReasoner separates sequence and structure embeddings whereas Qwen intermixes them.

key_findings.finding: The two-stage self-bootstrapped post-training (intra-domain grounding then cross-domain consolidation) improves both first-sample accuracy and reasoning quality over a naive coldstart.
key_findings.evidence: Pass@1 rises and pass@10−pass@1 gaps shrink: retrosynthesis 0.41→0.49→0.72 with gap 0.36→0.26→0.09; GO 0.48→0.52→0.59; QMOF 2.71→4.76 and 6.80→8.61 with gaps 11.29→4.07 and 13.82→5.57; LLM-judge score distributions shift up by +3.10 (DUD-E), +1.79 (GO), +1.61 (QMOF), +0.48 (retrosynthesis).

key_findings.finding: Structural-token chain-of-thought produces traces that human experts strongly prefer over a frontier LLM's and that can be audited against the physical object.
key_findings.evidence: Double-blind expert evaluation (N=177): tie-or-better in 98% of judgements (73% strongly prefer), per-axis means 8.7 vs 4.3 overall with all axes significant (Wilcoxon P<0.001); retrosynthesis traces follow analysis→disconnection→verification→feasibility and recover gold reactants in 5/5 illustrative USPTO-50K cases vs 2/5 for RSGPT and Opus-4.7; GO attention aligns with DNA-binding sites (AUROC 0.78-0.91, 3.1-4.2x top-20% enrichment).
